**Merge keeps both histories. Rebase rewrites yours.**

A merge adds one new commit that joins two branches. Nothing already committed changes.

A rebase replays your commits on top of another branch. Same edits, new commits, new IDs.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph M[merge]
    a[main] --> m((merge commit))
    b[your branch] --> m
  end
  subgraph R[rebase]
    c[main] --> d[copy of commit 1] --> e[copy of commit 2]
  end
```

Reach for rebase on your own branch that nobody else has pulled. History stays a straight line and reads easily.

Reach for merge once someone else has your branch, or when you want the record of what really happened.

The one hard rule: never rebase commits other people already pulled. Their copy and yours stop matching.
